values.title: Biological organism
values.text: The species is fundamentally biological, even if it also uses implants or engineered components.

values.title: Synthetic organism
values.text: The species is fundamentally artificial or synthetic rather than a biological organism.

values.title: One organism or body
values.text: One ordinary individual is one organism or body with one continuous personal identity.

values.title: Composite or symbiotic individual
values.text: One person is formed by two or more biologically distinct components acting as one individual.

values.title: Colonial individual
values.text: One person is a colony of many constituent organisms or modules whose combined activity forms the individual.

values.title: One mind across several bodies
values.text: One continuous mind is distributed across several physically separate bodies.

values.title: Several linked minds
values.text: Several distinct minds remain individuals while sharing a persistent cognitive network.

values.title: Emergent hive intelligence
values.text: The larger colony or hive has cognition that emerges above the constituent organisms.

values.title: Assimilative collective
values.text: The collective can incorporate outside individuals or organisms into its shared identity or network.

values.title: Persistent ordinary body
values.text: Personal continuity normally remains with one persistent body.

values.title: Replaceable or modular body
values.text: A person can move between or replace major body shells without ending personal continuity.

values.title: Projected body anchored to a core
values.text: The visible body is projected or generated by a persistent identity-bearing core or substrate.

values.title: Ordinary material body
values.text: The body is made primarily from ordinary matter rather than a persistent field, energy pattern, or exotic material.

values.title: Field, energy, or exotic-material body
values.text: The ordinary body is primarily a field, energy pattern, or other nonstandard material substrate.

values.title: Habitat-bound body
values.text: The body normally lives within a planetary, constructed, or otherwise bounded habitat rather than open space or vacuum.

values.title: Naturally space-native body
values.text: The ordinary body is naturally adapted to open space or vacuum rather than a planetary atmosphere.

values.title: One standard form
values.text: Most members share one ordinary body plan; individual differences stay within that form.

values.title: Individually variable form
values.text: Individuals vary substantially in body form without falling into a small set of recurring morphs.

values.title: Distinct recurring morphs
values.text: The species has several recurring morphs with inherited or stable body differences.

values.title: Biological castes
values.text: The species has recurring biological castes whose bodies or physiology differ by caste.

values.title: Life-stage forms
values.text: Major body form depends on life stage.

values.title: Birth-condition forms
values.text: Birth, gestation, or other early-development conditions determine which recurring form develops.

values.title: Environment-triggered forms
values.text: Environmental conditions can determine or switch a recurring body form.

values.title: Headless organization
values.text: The species has no single anatomical head. Major sensory and feeding structures are distributed elsewhere.

values.title: Multiple heads
values.text: The normal adult body has two or more heads.

values.title: Single head
values.text: The normal adult body has one primary head.
